message.content:
The sea usually looks **blue**—that’s because water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange) more strongly than shorter ones (blue). When sunlight hits it, the short‑wave light scatters off molecules and tiny particles, giving the ocean its characteristic hue.

But the “color” isn’t fixed:

| Condition | Typical Appearance |
|-----------|--------------------|
| Clear tropical waters | Bright turquoise / aquamarine |
| Shallow sandy bottoms | Greenish‑yellow or pale green |
| Deep open ocean | Dark navy or deep indigo |
| Algal blooms | Reddish‑brown or greenish tint |
| Stormy weather | Gray/blackish |
| Sunset/sunrise | Orange/pink hues along horizons |

So while we often think of the sea as blue, its actual shade depends on depth, clarity, angle of light, suspended matter, and even time of day!
